title: The gate suite is invoked as one Node entry point that any CI provider can run
asA: operator picking or moving between CI providers on an rcf-lite project
iWant: the gate suite to be a plain Node script the CI job invokes with one line
soThat: moving from one provider to another is a rewrite of the trigger definition, not a rewrite of the gates

acceptanceCriteria.description: The gate runner is a single Node entry point on disk under the project's tree (a script or module invocable as `node <path>` with no shell glue). The runner's file path is the same on every host.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the project tree at the head commit
acceptanceCriteria.when: the aggregate report is written by any CI run
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aggregate report's `runner.entryPoint` field records a project-relative path to a `.js` or `.mjs` file that exists at that path in the tree

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CI provider's job definition invokes the gate runner with a single command line: a `node <path>` invocation (or a package-manager script that resolves to the same). No gate-specific logic sits inside the CI provider's job definition.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the project's CI configuration file(s) committed under source control
acceptanceCriteria.when: an operator reads the job step that produces the pipeline report
acceptanceCriteria.then: the step is a single-line invocation of the Node entry point (or an equivalent package-manager script), and every gate-level branching, timing, and report-writing responsibility lives inside the Node runner rather than the CI configuration

acceptanceCriteria.description: A gate that names an unknown executable in its command array (a `command[0]` that does not resolve on the PATH) is refused at gate spawn with a stable-coded GATE_SPAWN_FAILED naming the executable and the gate name; the runner does not continue with other gates until the operator resolves.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a gate descriptor with command ["nonexistent-bin","arg"] and a runner invoked against the descriptor
acceptanceCriteria.when: the runner attempts to spawn the gate
acceptanceCriteria.then: the gate reports failed with GATE_SPAWN_FAILED naming the executable and the gate; the per-gate report is written failed; the aggregate reflects the failure
